Option 1: "دست همه اهل کشف و ارباب شهود - از دامن ادراک تو کوتاه بود" Rough translation: "The hand of all seekers of discovery and masters of insight - was too short from the hem of your perception." This seems to say that all seekers of knowledge, masters of insight, are limited by your perception? Maybe it's about the limited nature of human understanding compared to divine perception? Could be about the insufficiency of human grasp.

Option 2: "در دهان هر زبان که گردان است - از ثنای توا ندر او جان است" Rough: "In the mouth of every tongue that is turning (speaking?) - from the duality of the One, his life is not within." Hard to parse. Might be about the idea that all tongues speak, but the essence of the One is beyond them. So maybe about unity beyond language.

Option 3: "خرد اندر جهان او نرسد - علم بر آستان او نرسد" Means "Wisdom does not reach within the world; knowledge does not reach his threshold." This seems to say that wisdom/knowledge cannot reach the divine or the ultimate reality. So similar to option 1: human knowledge limited.

Option 4: "تو را چون شناسم منِ ناشناس - چو بیرونی از عقل و وهم و قیاس" Means "I know you like an unknown person, like an outsider from reason, illusion, and analogy." This seems to say that the speaker cannot know the person, they are unknown, outside reason and illusion. This is about the unknowability of the divine? Or the unknown.

This seems less about human limitation, more about the nature of the One beyond duality. But still could be about the same theme: the inability of human language to capture the One.
